title: Regular and irregular verbs
metaTitle: Irregular Italian verbs list: present, past participle and imperfect – Reference – icanspeak Italian
description: Regular and irregular Italian verbs at a glance: the io form of the present, the past participle and the io form of the imperfect, grouped by pattern, with the auxiliary for the passato prossimo.
lead: Three forms tell you most of what you need about an Italian verb: io in the present, the past participle (for the passato prossimo) and io in the imperfect. Verbs that behave in the same way are grouped together.
practice: Practise the passato prossimo with avere
Practise the passato prossimo with essere

sections.name: Regular verbs
sections.what: Take the ending off the infinitive (-are, -ere, -ire) and add the regular endings. Most verbs work like this, and new verbs do too: chattare, chatto, chattato, chattavo.
regel: Pattern: *parlare: parlo · parlato · parlavo.* *credere: credo · creduto · credevo.* *dormire: dormo · dormito · dormivo.*
The participle ends in -ato (-are), -uto (-ere) or -ito (-ire). The imperfect ends in -avo, -evo or -ivo.
Most verbs make the passato prossimo with *avere*: *ho parlato, ho creduto.* Verbs of movement and change take *essere*: *sono partito, sono salita.* The note says which.
With *essere* the participle agrees with the subject: *Maria è partita, loro sono partiti.* With *avere* it stays the same.

sections.name: Irregular verbs
sections.what: These change in one or more of the three forms. The most common verbs in Italian are here, so learn them first.
regel: The irregular participles are the ones to learn: *fare → fatto, dire → detto, prendere → preso, mettere → messo, leggere → letto, scrivere → scritto, vedere → visto, aprire → aperto.*
Some verbs are irregular only in the io form of the present, with -g- or -gg-: *venire → vengo, tenere → tengo, uscire → esco, rimanere → rimango.* The *noi* form is regular: *veniamo, teniamo.*
The imperfect is regular for nearly every verb. The exceptions come from an old stem: *essere → ero, fare → facevo, dire → dicevo, bere → bevevo, tradurre → traducevo.*
*Essere* and *stare* have the same participle, *stato*, and both take *essere*: *Sono stato a Roma.*
Modal verbs usually take the auxiliary of the verb that follows: *Ho dovuto lavorare, but Sono dovuto andare via.* In everyday speech *avere* is also common.

sections.name: Verbs in -isc- and spelling changes
sections.what: Many -ire verbs add -isc- in the present, and verbs in -care, -gare, -ciare and -giare change their spelling to keep the sound. The forms are regular otherwise.
regel: *-isc-* verbs: *finire → finisco, finisci, finisce, finiamo, finite, finiscono.* Only noi and voi have no -isc-. The participle and the imperfect are regular: *finito, finivo.*
There is no rule for which -ire verbs take -isc-: *dormire, partire, sentire, aprire* do not; *finire, capire, preferire, pulire, spedire* do. Learn them with the verb.
Verbs in *-care* and *-gare* add h before e and i to keep the hard sound: *cercare → cerco, cerchi, cerchiamo; pagare → pago, paghi, paghiamo.*
Verbs in *-ciare*, *-giare* drop the i before another i or e: *cominciare → comincio, cominci, cominciamo; mangiare → mangio, mangi, mangiamo.*
The imperfect and the participle keep the sound with the plain endings: *cercavo, cercato; mangiavo, mangiato.*
